body.objective: Add exact finite-dimensional Lie representation and invariant-theory machinery above tensor, wigner, harmonic, qext and Groebner. The immediate consumers are sf:program/work/observer-ward-cokernel-irrep-decomposition, sf:program/work/bridge-residual-atlas-branch-manifest and sf:program/work/quantum-parity-odd-third-curvature-carrier-manifest. Conflux can currently rediscover matrix blocks, ranks and incidences, but it cannot identify a block as an irreducible module, prove a tensor ansatz complete, or distinguish a selection-rule zero from an accidental coefficient cancellation outside the SU(2) coupling slice.
body.stop_condition: Provide typed reductive Lie algebras and finite-dimensional modules over Q or declared algebraic extensions; roots, weights, highest-weight modules, characters, Weyl dimension checks, tensor products, duals, symmetric/exterior powers, branching to declared subalgebras, invariant and equivariant Hom spaces, Young symmetrizers and Molien/Hilbert-series counts for bounded polynomial degree. Return explicit intertwiners, projectors, multiplicity spaces and completeness witnesses. Reproduce the existing SU(2) Clebsch-Gordan controls, decompose one Berger Ward cokernel under its stabilizer, and independently count and construct one parity-even and one single-epsilon curvature carrier. Export modules and intertwiners through a canonical Conflux IR so proposed structural identifications must replay exact commutator and completeness checks.
body.forbid: no floating character matching as an exact irrep identification; no hard-coded physics branch labels; no finite list of guessed tensors called a complete invariant basis without a dimension/Hilbert-series witness; no SU(2)-only API presented as general reductive invariant theory; no source verdict imported into Conflux rules; no producer projector reused as the independent verifier
notes: Priority A. This is the main missing semantic layer between exact matrices and meaningful representation-theoretic structure discovery.
A bounded first release covering sl2/SU2, so3, direct sums, declared stabilizer subalgebras and low-degree tensor invariants is sufficient if unsupported cases fail closed.
